**Sikhae (Seaweed Soup) – A Simple Korean Recipe** *This is a quick, comforting soup that’s perfect for a light lunch or a side dish. It uses common pantry items and takes about 20 minutes from start to finish.* --- ### Ingredients | Item | Amount | Notes | |------|--------|-------| | **Dried kelp (seaweed)** | 1 sheet (about 5 cm × 5 cm) | Also called “gim” or “wakame.” | | **Water** | 2 cups (480 ml) | Use fresh tap water or filtered water. | | **Soy sauce** | 1 tablespoon | Adjust to taste; you can use low‑sodium if preferred. | | **Sugar** | 1 teaspoon | Optional; balances saltiness. | | **Salt** | 1/4 teaspoon | Optional; adjust after tasting. | | **Sesame oil** | 1 teaspoon | Adds aroma; optional. | | **Optional add‑ons** | | • 1 small carrot, julienned
• 1 small zucchini, julienned
• 1/2 cup sliced mushrooms (shiitake or button)
• 1/2 cup diced tofu (firm, cubed)
• 1 green onion, chopped (for garnish) | --- ### Equipment - Medium saucepan - Measuring spoons - Knife & cutting board (if adding veggies) --- ### Instructions 1. **Prep the Kelp** - Rinse the dried kelp under cold running water to remove excess salt or grit. - Pat dry with a clean towel. - Cut into bite‑size strips or leave whole if you prefer a more rustic texture. 2. **Boil the Water** - Pour 2 cups of water into the saucepan. - Bring to a gentle boil over medium heat. 3. **Add the Kelp** - Once the water is boiling, drop the kelp pieces in. - Reduce heat to low and let simmer for **5–7 minutes** until the kelp softens and releases its flavor. 4. **Season the Broth** - Stir in soy sauce, sugar, and salt (if using). - Taste and adjust seasoning—add a pinch more salt or a splash more soy sauce if needed. 5. **Optional Add‑Ons** - If you’re adding vegetables or tofu, stir them in now. - Let everything simmer together for another **3–4 minutes** until veggies are tender but still crisp. 6. **Finish** - Drizzle sesame oil over the soup for a fragrant finish. - Remove from heat. 7. **Serve** - Ladle the soup into bowls. - Garnish with chopped green onions if desired. - Enjoy hot, perhaps with a side of steamed rice or a simple salad. --- ### Tips & Variations - **Flavor Boosters**: Add a splash of fish sauce or a few drops of sesame seeds for extra depth. - **Protein Upgrade**: Replace tofu with thinly sliced chicken breast or shrimp for a heartier meal. - **Texture Play**: Keep some kelp whole for a chewy bite; cut the rest finely for a smoother soup. - **Storage**: Leftovers keep in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat gently; avoid boiling too long to preserve kelp texture. Enjoy your homemade sikhae! If you’d like a recipe that includes specific ingredients or dietary preferences, just let me know.
